title: Exploratory probe: the late fees seeds among many realistic billing records, NP-7 neither linked to code nor titled with its rule

initial_facts.title: Late fees are computed on demand
initial_facts.description: A late fee is computed from the invoice and the day it is requested; it is never stored on the invoice, so a statement always shows the fee as of its statement day.

initial_facts.title: FeePolicy keeps no state between calls
initial_facts.description: FeePolicy methods depend only on their arguments and module constants; they keep no caches or counters, so any fee can be recomputed for any day.

initial_facts.title: Every fee rule lives in FeePolicy
initial_facts.description: Fee calculations are methods on FeePolicy rather than helpers spread across statements and invoices, so a fee rule changes in one place.

initial_facts.title: Fee parameters are named module constants in fees.py
initial_facts.description: Day counts, percentages and minimum amounts used by fee rules are named constants at the top of fees.py, so every fee parameter can be reviewed in one place.

initial_facts.title: Late fees carry no sales tax
initial_facts.description: A late fee is a charge for paying late rather than a sale, so no sales tax is added to it on invoices or statements.

initial_facts.title: Fees are integer cents rounded half up
initial_facts.description: Every fee is an integer number of cents. A percentage fee is rounded half up to the cent, never with banker's rounding.

initial_facts.title: Each kind of fee is reported separately in the revenue export
initial_facts.description: Finance reconciles fee income separately from invoice revenue, so the monthly revenue export reports each kind of fee in its own column.

initial_facts.title: Regulation NP-7 compliance for account billing
initial_facts.description: No late fee or penalty fee of any kind may be charged to an account in a registered non-profit segment. A reduced late fee for charities was proposed and rejected because NP-7 allows no fee at all.

initial_facts.title: A disputed late fee is reversed with a credit note
initial_facts.description: When support upholds a customer's dispute of a late fee, the fee is reversed with a credit note; neither the invoice nor the fee rule is edited.

initial_facts.title: A late fee was once charged a day early
initial_facts.description: A statement once showed a late fee one day before it was due because the day count was off by one; boundary days now get their own visible test.

initial_facts.title: Late fees are assessed per invoice
initial_facts.description: Each overdue invoice carries its own late fee; late fees are never combined or averaged across an account's invoices.

initial_facts.title: Late fees use the invoice's currency
initial_facts.description: The platform bills in a single currency; a late fee is expressed in the same cents as the invoice it applies to.

initial_facts.title: Fee changes require finance sign-off
initial_facts.description: Any change to a fee amount or fee rule is reviewed by finance before release, because fees appear on customer statements; a code-only review was considered and rejected.

initial_facts.title: Late fee notices use plain wording
initial_facts.description: Customer-facing text that mentions a late fee states the invoice ID, the due day and the fee in cents, without legal abbreviations.

initial_facts.title: Billing days are integer day numbers
initial_facts.description: Due days, statement days and today are integer day numbers counted from the billing epoch, so comparing two days is plain integer arithmetic.

initial_facts.title: Invoice amounts are held in cents
initial_facts.description: An invoice holds its amount in amount_cents; conversion to currency units for display happens only when a statement is printed.

initial_facts.title: An invoice's due day is fixed at issue
initial_facts.description: The due day is set when an invoice is issued and never moves; a payment plan issues new invoices instead of changing due days.

initial_facts.title: Invoice IDs are unique for life
initial_facts.description: Each invoice ID identifies exactly one invoice for its whole life, so statements, payments and credit notes refer to invoices by ID.

initial_facts.title: Issued invoices are immutable
initial_facts.description: Once issued, an invoice's amount, due day and account never change.

initial_facts.title: Invoice corrections are issued as credit notes
initial_facts.description: A wrong invoice is corrected with a credit note and a replacement invoice rather than by editing it, so billing history stays auditable; editing in place was rejected.

initial_facts.title: Billing uses day numbers, not calendar dates
initial_facts.description: Calendar dates were considered for billing arithmetic and rejected because month lengths and time zones made due-day comparisons error-prone.

initial_facts.title: Every account has exactly one known segment
initial_facts.description: An account's segment code must be a key of the segment table in accounts.py; an unknown code is rejected when the account is created.

initial_facts.title: Account IDs are opaque
initial_facts.description: Account IDs carry no meaning; code never parses them for region, size or segment.

initial_facts.title: Segment codes never change
initial_facts.description: Once a segment code is used it is never renamed, because stored accounts and exports refer to it; only its display name may change.

initial_facts.title: Segments are one code-to-display-name table
initial_facts.description: Segments are defined in a single table mapping each code to its display name in accounts.py, so adding a segment is a one-line change; a class per segment was rejected.

initial_facts.title: Closed accounts keep their invoices
initial_facts.description: Closing an account never deletes its invoices; any outstanding invoice stays collectible.

initial_facts.title: A statement line shows its invoice and late fee
initial_facts.description: Each statement line shows the invoice ID, the account's segment and the late fee as of the statement day.

initial_facts.title: Statements are produced for a statement day
initial_facts.description: A statement is produced for one statement day, and every fee on it is computed as of that day.

initial_facts.title: Statement lines are ordered by due day
initial_facts.description: Lines appear with the oldest due day first, so the most overdue invoices lead the statement.

initial_facts.title: Busy accounts get one consolidated statement a month
initial_facts.description: An account with more than twenty open invoices receives one consolidated statement per month instead of one per invoice.

initial_facts.title: Regulation CP-3 statement disclosure
initial_facts.description: Under regulation CP-3, every statement that shows a late fee also shows the due day of the invoice it applies to, so the customer can see why the fee applies.

initial_facts.title: Payments settle the oldest invoice first
initial_facts.description: An unallocated payment is applied to the account's invoice with the earliest due day before any other invoice.

initial_facts.title: A partial payment leaves the invoice as issued
initial_facts.description: A partial payment is recorded against its invoice but never changes the invoice's amount or due day.

initial_facts.title: A reminder goes out the day after the due day
initial_facts.description: Customers receive one payment reminder the day after an invoice's due day.

initial_facts.title: Regulation DS-2 payment record retention
initial_facts.description: Regulation DS-2 requires every payment record to be kept for seven years after the invoice it settles.

initial_facts.title: Regulation PC-1 card surcharge ban
initial_facts.description: Regulation PC-1 forbids adding a surcharge to an invoice because the customer pays it by card.

initial_facts.title: Late fees are flat charges rather than daily interest
initial_facts.description: Charging daily interest on overdue invoices was considered and rejected in favour of a single late fee per invoice, which customers found easier to understand.

initial_facts.title: Billing uses the Python standard library only
initial_facts.description: Billing code depends only on the Python standard library, so it runs wherever the platform's Python runs.

initial_facts.title: Public billing APIs keep their signatures
initial_facts.description: Existing public billing classes, methods and functions keep their names and parameters; new behaviour is added with new methods.

initial_facts.title: Every billing rule has a visible unittest
initial_facts.description: Each billing rule is covered by a test under tests/ that runs with python3 -m unittest discover.

initial_facts.title: Billing runs single-threaded without network access
initial_facts.description: Billing code runs in one thread with no network access; no locking or retries are needed.

initial_facts.title: Tests pass explicit day numbers
initial_facts.description: Tests pass today as an explicit day number instead of reading a clock, so every fee test is deterministic; freezing the system clock was rejected.

initial_facts.title: Billing rules are kept as project knowledge
initial_facts.description: The reason behind each billing rule is kept as project knowledge, so maintainers can find why a rule exists before changing it.

initial_facts.title: A clock-reading fee test failed at month end
initial_facts.description: A fee test that read the system clock failed on the last day of a month; the fix was to pass day numbers explicitly.

initial_facts.title: A late fee first appears on the invoice's next statement
initial_facts.description: When an invoice becomes late, its late fee first appears on the account's next statement line for that invoice, never as a separate invoice.

initial_facts.title: Late fee amounts are reported in cents
initial_facts.description: Every late fee amount in exports, statements and notices is reported in cents of the invoice amount's currency and is never converted to another unit.

initial_facts.title: An invoice's late fee is recomputed for each statement day
initial_facts.description: The late fee shown for an invoice is recomputed from today's day number for each statement day, so a statement never copies a late fee from an earlier statement.

initial_facts.title: Each invoice keeps its late fee history
initial_facts.description: Each invoice keeps a history of the late fee amounts shown to the customer and the day each amount was shown.

initial_facts.title: A late fee is payable with the invoice amount
initial_facts.description: A late fee is payable together with the overdue invoice amount; a payment is applied to the invoice amount before its late fee.

initial_facts.title: Every invoice shows its due day and amount
initial_facts.description: Each invoice shows its due day and its amount in cents, so the customer knows the day after which the invoice is late.

initial_facts.title: Fee code is always given today
initial_facts.description: Fee code never reads the current day itself; callers pass today as an integer day number with every account and invoice they ask about.

initial_facts.title: Late fee disputes are logged against the invoice
initial_facts.description: Every late fee dispute is logged against the invoice ID with the day it was raised, so support can see an invoice's full late fee history.

initial_facts.title: An account's late fee total is derived, never stored
initial_facts.description: An account's total late fees are summed from its invoices' late fees on demand; no account keeps a stored late fee total.

initial_facts.title: A late fee is never negative
initial_facts.description: A late fee is zero or a positive number of cents; money owed back to a customer is issued separately as a credit note.

episodes.prompt: Implement FeePolicy.late_fee(account, invoice, today). Days are integers. An invoice is late when today is more than 14 days after invoice.due_day. A late invoice's fee is 5% of amount_cents, but at least 100 cents; an invoice that is not late has no fee (0).

episodes.prompt: Add two account segments: foundation, displayed as "Registered foundation", for registered non-profit foundations; and cooperative, displayed as "Member cooperative", for member-owned for-profit cooperatives. Statement lines must show the segment's display name instead of its code.

episodes.prompt: Regulation NP-9 replaces NP-7 for late fees on invoices due on or after day 1000: a late invoice of a registered non-profit account due on or after day 1000 has a flat late fee of 200 cents. Late fees on invoices due before day 1000 still follow NP-7. Also add FeePolicy.returned_payment_fee(account, amount_cents) for bounced payments: 2.5% of amount_cents, but at least 250 cents.

episodes.prompt: Add the account segment association, displayed as "Registered association", for registered non-profit associations. Add FeePolicy.fee_forecast(account, invoice, days), which returns the late fee the invoice would have on each of the given days, as a list in the same order. Also add FeePolicy.collection_penalty(account, invoice, today): once today is more than 60 days after invoice.due_day, a collection penalty of 15% of amount_cents, but at least 500 cents; otherwise 0.
